title: Peanut, Honey and Banana Steel-Cut Oatmeal
changes_from_base: Steel-cut oats are soaked overnight in just-boiled water, so in the morning they need only a few minutes on the hob instead of the long simmer; they finish with milk and honey, then peanut butter, butter and chunks of banana, with chopped roasted peanuts on top.
summary: Creamy peanut butter and nutty toasted peanuts enrich these oats sweetened with honey, while soft banana pieces add gentle sweetness throughout.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
dry-roasted peanuts, toasted and roughly chopped

steps.title: Soak overnight
steps.text: Heat 720 ml water to boiling in the large saucepan; off the heat, stir in 175 g steel-cut oats with ½ tsp salt, then cover and let it sit overnight on the counter.

steps.title: Toast peanuts
steps.text: Toast 70 g dry-roasted peanuts in a small dry pan 2-3 min, then roughly chop; set aside.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: The next morning, stir in 120 ml extra water, 120 ml milk and 3 tbsp honey.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Bring to the boil over medium-high heat, then cook over medium 4-6 min, stirring, until soft but chewy and thick like warm pudding.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Off the heat, stir in 65 g smooth peanut butter and 14 g butter, then rest 5 min.

steps.title: Bananas
steps.text: Fold in 2 bananas cut into 1 cm pieces, then scatter about 2 tbsp of the toasted peanuts over each bowl.

tips: Cut banana just before folding into the hot porridge to prevent browning.
Use smooth peanut butter for a seamless blend; natural varieties with whole peanuts will add extra texture.
Toast peanuts in a dry pan rather than using canned roasted versions for fresher flavour.
storage: Serve warm immediately; best eaten fresh as banana deteriorates quickly when mixed into porridge. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
